::: {.callout-important title="Status — skeleton, not a draft"}

Section order, headings and the mandatory Design Table follow the *Nature
Ecology & Evolution* Stage 1 template (`np-nee-template-stage1.pdf`, this
directory). All scientific content is a placeholder.

Hypotheses, the operational definition of connectivity, the sampling plan and
the model specification are developed outside this repository and arrive here
already decided (CLAUDE.md, *Roles*). They must be written in by an author,
not inferred from the protocols.

Delete this callout before submission.

:::

# Abstract {.unnumbered}

::: {.callout-note}

**PLACEHOLDER — max 150 words, no references.**

Per the template, the abstract should:

1. open with one sentence introducing the general topic and its significance
   for a broad audience;
2. state the specific research questions;
3. state what will be done;
4. state broadly what results would confirm or disconfirm the hypotheses.

It will be lightly revised at Stage 2 to include results.

:::

# Introduction

::: {.callout-note}

**PLACEHOLDER.** No subheadings are permitted in this section.

Required content:

- Review of the literature motivating the research question.
- Full description of the experimental aims and research questions.
- Each research question motivated, explained, and linked to specific
  hypotheses and predictions.
- Predictions defined precisely in terms of the specific independent and
  dependent variables. Numbering as Hypothesis 1, Hypothesis 2 … with a
  corresponding H0 in each case is recommended.
- Commitment to an interpretation of **all** potential data patterns, including
  those running counter to prediction. Absence of evidence cannot be
  interpreted as evidence of absence under NHST; interpreting non-predicted
  patterns requires Bayesian inference or frequentist equivalence testing.
- A call-out to the mandatory Design Table (@tbl-design).

Constraints on wording:

- Write the proposed research in the **future tense** throughout.
- If the evidence is correlational or cross-sectional, use no causal language
  and no language implying causality.
- No priority or novelty claims, anywhere in the manuscript.

:::

# Methods

## Ethics information

::: {.callout-note}

**PLACEHOLDER.** This research involves non-human animals, so the Methods
section must open with a statement that:

- the research complies with all relevant ethical regulations;
- names the board and institution that approved the study protocol
  (WP1 Pallasjärvi, Finland; WP2 Grimsö, Sweden — permits differ by
  jurisdiction and both must be named);
- confirms that the ARRIVE guidelines were used to report the research.

:::

## Pilot data

::: {.callout-note}

**PLACEHOLDER — include only if applicable.**

- Describe pilot studies and results briefly here; report them in full in
  Supplementary Information.
- Pilot data and custom analysis code must be deposited and referred to in the
  Data availability and Code availability statements. They must be accessible
  for peer review, and may be embargoed until Stage 2 acceptance.
- Simulated data supporting a power analysis must also be made available.
- Any NHST reported on pilot data must be reported in full:
  statistic(df) = value, *p* = value, effect size = value, % CI = values.

:::

## Design

::: {.callout-note}

**PLACEHOLDER.** Experimental procedures in sufficient detail for another
researcher to repeat the methodology exactly, using only this protocol, the
Supplementary Information, and the linked code and data.

Must include:

- Full description of outcome-neutral criteria and positive controls — quality
  checks orthogonal to the experimental hypotheses (e.g. absence of floor or
  ceiling effects, positive controls).
- A statement on randomization, if applicable.
- For experimental studies, whether the design is within-subjects,
  between-subjects, mixed, or other.
- A statement on blinding. If there will be no blinding, state exactly:
  "Data collection and analysis will not be performed blind to the conditions
  of the experiments."

Source material — check currency before reusing, and note that the funded
proposal is *not* the current plan (CLAUDE.md):

- `../protocols/pallasjarvi-fieldwork-protocol.qmd` (WP1 field design)
- `../protocols/grimso-field-protocol.qmd` (WP2 longitudinal design, RFID
  contact triangulation)
- `../protocols/pilot-lab-protocol.qmd` (extraction, PacBio HiFi 16S)
- `../protocols/data-management-plan.qmd` (sample IDs, batch design, and the
  operational definition of connectivity)

:::

## Sampling plan

::: {.callout-note}

**PLACEHOLDER.**

If any hypothesis is tested by Neyman–Pearson inference:

- A statistical power analysis is required, with effect sizes justified from
  the existing literature and based on the **lowest** available or meaningful
  estimate (published estimates are inflated by publication bias).
- A priori power must be **≥ 0.95** for every proposed hypothesis test.

If any hypothesis is tested by Bayes factors:

- Specify the predictions of the theory such that a Bayes factor can be
  computed — which distribution represents the theory, and how its parameters
  are set.
- Commit to collecting data until BF ≥ 10 in favour of the experimental
  hypothesis or the null. A maximum feasible sample size may be specified given
  resource limits, but it must be large enough that an inconclusive result at
  that size would still be an important message for the field.

Regardless of method, list:

- all data inclusion and exclusion criteria, and how they affect the sampling
  strategy;
- a full description of proposed sample characteristics;
- objective procedures for exclusion due to technical error or other reasons,
  including how and under what conditions data would be replaced.

These details must also be summarised in @tbl-design.

:::

## Analysis plan

::: {.callout-note}

**PLACEHOLDER.**

- All pre-processing steps, and a precise description of every planned
  analysis, including correction for multiple comparisons if applicable.
- All covariates and regressors stated.
- Where an analysis decision is contingent on the outcome of a prior analysis,
  the contingency must be specified as an IF–THEN rule and then adhered to.
- **Do not** include exploratory analyses here. They belong in the Stage 2
  manuscript under an *Exploratory Analyses* heading.

After in-principle acceptance, any deviation from this section requires
editorial approval **before** it is implemented.

:::

::: {.callout-note}

Requirements for @tbl-design:

- **Exact** correspondence between each scientific hypothesis and each
  statistical test.
- Hypotheses must name the measure and the predicted direction. Not
  "Condition A will affect performance differently from Condition B", but
  e.g. "Reaction times will be significantly higher in Condition A than in
  Condition B".
- Analysis strategies contingent on results (e.g. normal vs. non-normal
  distributions) must be given as IF–THEN statements.
- Null results cannot be interpreted under NHST. Interpreting them requires a
  commitment to Bayes factors or equivalence testing.

:::
